newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Blast kills man at Kinshasa airport, bomb suspected.
newsitem.headline: Blast kills man at Kinshasa airport, bomb suspected.

text.p: An explosion killed one man in Kinshasa's international airport early on Monday, airport officials said.
Airline sources said it looked as though the cause was a bomb.

It was not immediately clear whether the blast, at a customs office adjoining an office of Zairean military intelligence, was linked to the revolt in the east or a personal grievance against the customs service.
The blast did not disrupt flights to and from the airport but Western airlines called for increased security.
The dead man, a retired Zairean telecommunications worker, was killed when a wall collapsed due to the 4 a.m. blast. A second man was slightly hurt.
Soldiers sealed the area off and launched an investigation.
One Western airline source said initial investigations suggested that the explosive TNT had been used.
"Zaire isn't used to the idea of terrorist attacks," he said. "They don't have any sophisticated laboratires to help their investigations."

"We don't know yet what caused the incident but it doesn't look like an accident," a senior airport official told Reuters. "It was lucky it happened during the night when there were few people around," he added.
Western airlines called for tighter security. They insisted that informal protocol fixers used by many passengers to smooth their arrival be banned.
Air France, Sabena, South African Airlines, Cameroon Airlines, Ethiopian Airlines and the Portuguese airline TAP run flights to the airport.
A Sabena flight landed an hour after the blast. Zaire Airlines, the main commercial airline in Zaire, said it would be running a normal schedule.
The senior airport officials said the dead man was a retired employee of the state telecommunications company who was at the airport to buy goods to trade in town.
Rebels, who took up arms in October, are fighting to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko. They hold a quarter of the sprawling Central African nation, mainly in the east and south.
